extDesc.message: Right-click a number, or click a tel: link: SimpleDial shows a QR code to call from your phone, or opens the tel: handler.

infoBox.message:
SimpleDial only recognizes numbers and hands them over — it never places the call itself, and it never modifies the page you are on.

What starts a call: right-click a tel: link or a number you selected and pick Call; or click the toolbar icon. A plain left-click on a tel: link can be routed through SimpleDial too, but that is off until you turn it on below.

Where it goes: either to the phone handler registered in your browser or system, or — with the QR option on — to a code you scan with your phone, built on this computer and sent nowhere.

Whenever a call goes through SimpleDial, the browser asks once for permission to open the external application and never asks again, on any site. Links you click without that option enabled keep asking per site, as usual.

recognitionHint.message: Regular expression applied to the candidate after removing spaces, dots, hyphens and brackets. Alternatives are separated with |. If it cannot be compiled, the default rules are used.

regexInvalid.message: Invalid expression — if saved, the default rules will be used.

testHint.message: Type a number as it would appear on a page to see whether it would be recognized with the rule currently set.

protocolHint.message: Scheme handed to the handler registered in the system. tel: is right almost always. Change it if your softphone only answers to another scheme: some clients register for callto: or sip:.

popupToggle.message: Open a dialing panel instead of the phone application

popupToggleHint.message: Off by default: clicking the icon opens your phone application straight away — a plain shortcut to the dialer, with or without the QR option. Turn it on to get a small panel where you can type a number that is not on the page.

popupHint.message: Leave the field empty to just open the phone application.

popupUnusual.message: Unusual format — it will be dialed anyway.

qrToggle.message: Show a QR code instead of opening the phone application

qrToggleHint.message: Instead of opening the computer's phone application, SimpleDial shows a QR code: point your phone's camera at it to start the call from there. The QR always uses tel:, whatever dialing protocol is set below.

qrScanHint.message: Point your phone's camera at the code to start the call.

qrNoNumber.message: No number — type one in the dialing panel.

popupQrHint.message: A QR code will open for this number.

interceptToggle.message: Handle left clicks on tel: links already present on the page

interceptToggleHint.message:
Off by default. Turn it on and a left-click on a tel: link goes through SimpleDial instead of the browser, ending up in whichever mode you chose above — exactly like right-click > Call.

Why you might want it: the browser asks for permission to open your phone application once, instead of asking again on every new site.

Why it is not on by default: that per-site prompt is a safety check, and skipping it should be your choice. Right-click > Call already goes through SimpleDial either way. The page is never modified, and holding Ctrl, Shift or Alt always falls back to the browser's normal behaviour.

handlersHint.message: Chrome lists at chrome://settings/handlers the web applications allowed to handle tel: and lets you revoke them. If the number is meant to reach a softphone installed on the computer, that association belongs to the operating system and does not appear here.

statusSavedInvalid.message: ✓ Saved — invalid expression, the default rules will be used

secNumbers.message: 1 · What counts as a phone number

protocolScope.message: Applies to calls placed from this computer. A QR code always encodes tel:, because phone cameras do not act on the other schemes.

badgeFailed.message: SimpleDial: the call could not be started

qrScope.message: Applies to every call SimpleDial starts: right-click > Call, the panel's Call button, and — if you turn it on below — a left-click on a tel: link.
